BiblicalUsage: Hekon means willingly, of one's own accord, and Paul uses it twice, once for himself and once for the whole creation. In 1 Corinthians 9:17 he says if I do this thing willingly I have a reward, and in Romans 8:20 the creature was made subject to vanity, not willingly, but by reason of him who subjected it in hope.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the contrast is the whole story of the fall and the gospel: creation did not choose its bondage, and Paul chose his service, and the hope is that the willing service undoes the unwilling bondage.
